thread.title: Market Volatility Bulletin: Nasdaq Manages Gains While S&P Slumps On Tariff Headlines

author: The Balance of Trade
title: Market Volatility Bulletin: Nasdaq Manages Gains While S&P Slumps On Tariff Headlines
text:
Market Intro
CNBC: 12:02 EST
US stocks ( SPY , DIA , IWM ) took a step back today with trade skirmishes back in the news . Risk assets are trying to recover the lost ground, but this particular headline has plagued equities going back to late February. As of noon EST on Thursday, the NASDAQ 100 index QQQ has managed to stay positive despite dour mood for the other mainline indexes.
Sector SPDRs
There's a certain amount of arbitrariness as to which sector suffers most. Overall consumer staples ( XLP ) have really had some setbacks in the past quarter, which is interesting given that the sector is traditionally viewed as one of the defensives. The tech sector ( XLK ) derives much of its revenue from overseas activity, and yet this part of the S&P is managing a gain.
Sovereign yields ( IEF , TLT , AGG ) are unchanged today, which may be a welcomed rest after the tear higher in the rip higher for 10-yr volatility from earlier in the week. If Treasury vol can get its footing, it may create headwinds for those looking to benefit from long-vol positioning ( VXX , UVXY , TVIX ).
Thoughts On Volatility
On Tuesday, the biggest losing sector in the US was the financial sector ( XLF ). Deutsche Bank, and really German banks overall, have quite a bit of potential first and second-order exposure to Italian debt. One can argue to what extent troubles in Europe bleed over to the US, but certainly the entire EU banking sector would feel the impact.
Many of the vol ETPs have a daily rebalancing schedule. As such, we must be careful of the compounding effect embedded in large moves. Daily rebalancing effectively creates a favorable convex effect, either in the case of losing less in adverse moves with momentum, or alternatively gaining more in the event of favorable swings with momentum. In either case, momentum is the friend of such ETPs (relative to no daily rebalancing).
"Narrative is equivalent to data"… in secondary markets narrative can be far more important than data. And this speaks to why an event that can prove so troublesome on one day can more or less dissipate the next (or, of course, vice versa). In both markets and politics, an open mind can foster a broader perspective.
Term Structure
Were the last 30 days a trick or a treat? 30-day HV now rests alongside the 10-day, which itself got something of a boost this week. The VX term structure is rather flat: 2 points total between the front and back of the curve. If we measure the volatility risk premium as spot VIX minus 30-day HV, we're getting a pretty large figure. Of course, this may not be a true reflection of VRP.
Trader memories can be short. Recall that back in late March into mid-April, volatility in the big name tech stocks like GOOG , FB , AMZN , AAPL were a large part of the redux in generalized vol over that period. At present NADSAQ volatility is still quite well behaved, barely taking the bait on Tuesday's session. Lower NASDAQ vol provides support for the short vol case ( SVXY ).
Speaking of, SVXY managed a small gain for just a bit during today's session, and this despite the fact that spot VIX has been higher throughout the day . This adds some additional fodder for consideration to Bill Valentine's tweet, highlighted earlier: SVXY does not move directly with spot VIX, but rather the M1 and M2 VX contracts, which have minds of their own, particularly when expiration is not right around the corner.
Conclusion If this is your first time reading Market Volatility Bulletin, thanks for giving it a try. If you're a regular, we thank you for your ongoing contributions in the comments section.
Georgy Uspenskiy shares his view on volatility and relative value in the prior MVB . I think the statement at the very end about watching fixed income could be the single most important detail (he mentions "exogenous events"… this is a likely transmission mechanism). The overall notion that the S&P more or less chops higher is quite reasonable given the stronger economic and fundamental data.
Thank you for reading.
